stem.text: Let \( y = f(x) \) be a twice-differentiable function. Suppose that \( f''(4) = 3 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \right|_{x=4} = 3 \), so the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y when x = 4 is 3.

worked_solution.text: In \( f''(4) \) the function is f, the independent variable is x, and the second derivative is evaluated at x = 4, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \right|_{x=4} = 3 \).
It says that the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y when x = 4 is 3.

options.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}} \right|_{x=4} = 3 \), so the rate of change, with respect to y, of the rate of change of x when x = 4 is 3.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable

options.label: \( \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = 3 \), so the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y, the same at every x, is 3.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the second derivative function

options.label: \( \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} = 3 \text{ at } x = 4 \), so the square of the rate of change of y with respect to x when x = 4 is 3.
options.derivation: the second derivative written as the square of the first derivative

options.label: \( \left. \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \right|_{x=4} = 3 \), so the rate of change, with respect to x, of the rate of change of y when x = 4 is 3.
